scope: Registry scope replacement, selected historical binding release and native startup/reap ownership. Complete protocol goal remains active.
implemented: Changed/removed explicit native instances retire their operations before replacement admission. Active executions receive native interrupt controls; metadata operations cancel. An exclusive barrier waits for admitted operations before native disposal. Cleanup is owned by a separate worker so abandoning a waiter cannot abandon reaping. Failed cleanup refuses replacement and may be retried.

Builtins in legacy routers use the same scope boundary. Adding an explicit builtin override closes its previous default scope; removal closes that override before the default reopens. Disposal selects one builtin rather than shutting down unrelated providers. Immutable scope snapshots prevent concurrent settings changes from bypassing managed admission via default discovery/refresh/quota routes.

The private binding index captures native owner keys and fresh binding IDs at binding events. Selection stages all planner-selected sessions, including historical bindings, while preserving target and stopped/error sessions. Historical background work refuses direct selection transactionally. Release ACKs mark the matching binding incarnation; retries and later rebinds do not reuse an old physical release receipt. Deletion purges routing metadata after native disposal.
Workspace planning now compares current live-session cwd against target worktree path with the source precedence rules; the service regression was red before the fix.

Codex discovery/quota probes participate in their owning instance actor scope. Disposal waits for child-process reap acknowledgements, including cancelled startup probes. Per shared-home startup gates serialize native SQLite initialization across probes, inference and account overlays, allowing independent homes to start concurrently. A cancelled handshake retains its gate until its actor is reaped. The overlap regression was red before the gate.
